creator: Alexander Terp
description:
Two halves of one gap in `TabInfo`, both measured against the pinned 0.8.0 (`corpus/herdr-0.8.0/naming/`, `docs/observations/herdr-0.8.0.md` section 16).

**A tab name cannot be cleared.** `tab.rename` declares `label` a required string where `pane.rename` declares it nullable, and `Tab::set_custom_name` wraps whatever it is given in `Some`. So null is a schema violation and empty leaves an empty name that survives a daemon restart:

    tab.list                 label "1"          herdr's own position number
    tab.rename "release"     label "release"
    tab.rename ""            label ""           and there is no way back to "1"

Muster gets away with it: `tab_label` already drops an all-digits label to suppress herdr's position number, so an empty label renders as the bare place, which is what an un-named tab renders as. herdr's own interface shows a blank tab.

**And a tab somebody names `42` reads as un-named.** That same all-digits test is the only way to tell a name from a number, because `TabInfo.label` is filled in either way and nothing beside it says which. Pre-existing, but newly reachable now that naming a tab is a menu item rather than a CLI call nobody made.

One fix covers both: either a nullable `label` on `tab.rename` plus a `custom_name` (or a `named` flag) on `TabInfo`, or a `TabInfo.label` that is null when nobody named it. The second is smaller and answers the question directly.

Low urgency, and the second half is the one that will actually be noticed - by whoever names a tab after a ticket number.
title: 🔌 Upstream: a tab cannot be un-named, and a tab named `42` disappears
